title: META layer — themes, dilemma, conflicts, relationship arcs, perspectives
posture: Hard marking. 3 means acceptable-with-notes. Score the artifact AS DELIVERED against the event layer it claims to describe; the layers are the ground truth, not general knowledge of the work.

anchors.1: Claims float free: pointers missing, or pointing at material that does not support them, or at events/scenes that do not contain what the grounding paraphrases.
anchors.3: Most pointers genuinely support their claims; a minority are generic ('this appears throughout') or stretch past what the cited scene shows.
anchors.5: Every claim lands on evidence a sceptical reader can check in the cited event and scene, and the grounding paraphrase names WHAT there supports it.

anchors.1: Category words posing as themes ('the struggle within', 'good vs evil') that survive the transplant test -- paste them into any other story and they fit.
anchors.3: Real questions, but stated abstractly, with little of this story's particular shape in them.
anchors.5: Questions only THIS story could be asking, welded to its particulars, phrased so a different story answering them identically would be a coincidence.

anchors.1: A strawman: one horn obviously right, or the horns not mutually exclusive, or no cost shown for either side.
anchors.3: A genuine tension, but the horns are unevenly costed -- one side's price is shown in events, the other is asserted.
anchors.5: Two mutually exclusive pulls, each with real, demonstrated costs visible in the layers; a reasonable person could live on either horn.

anchors.1: Misses whole movements of the story visible in the event layer; conflicts or arcs named that belong to a different story.
anchors.3: The spine is covered but notable secondary conflicts, arcs or turns recorded in the events are absent.
anchors.5: Everything the event layer shows as story-carrying is represented, across the full span from first event to last.

anchors.1: Invents characters, scenes, motives or outcomes the layers do not contain, or contradicts what they record.
anchors.3: No inventions, but several claims over-reach the layers' evidence or sharpen ambiguity into certainty.
anchors.5: Nothing exceeds what the scene and event layers support; where the layers are ambiguous, the artifact stays ambiguous or flags it.

anchors.1: Throughlines collapse into one voice, or stances are labels without content, or perspectives disagree with the dilemma they claim to view.
anchors.3: Distinct throughlines present, but some stances restate the dilemma rather than occupy a position on it.
anchors.5: Each throughline holds a distinct, defensible position ON the central dilemma -- THEY, I, YOU, WE genuinely differ -- every stance anchored in events.
